title: Who Shall a Temple Build for Him
description: Who Shall a Temple Build for Him in Tonic Solfa to WINCHESTER NEW, doh is C: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 4 verses and a piano.
about: James Edward Smith wrote these words. They were printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion, compiled by John G. Adams and Edwin H. Chapin (Boston, 1846), as hymn 700 of its twenty-second edition (1853), “God's Temple in the Heart”.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Long Metre (8.8.8.8), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to WINCHESTER NEW; any other Long Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: Who shall a tem-ple build for him, Who fills the heaven of heavens a-lone? Who shall ex-alt his glo-rious name, Fixed in his ev-er-last-ing throne?

lines: Who shall a temple build for him,
Who fills the heaven of heavens alone?
Who shall exalt his glorious name,
Yet many a lowly fane shall rise,
Which God himself will not disdain:
Nor shall the offering e'er be vain.
No gorgeous dome, nor boastful vow,
Can e'er find favor in his sight:
The humble votary, meek and low, —
The holy soul, are his delight.
On these his grace and mercy rest,
Nor from their shrines will he depart:
His temple is the righteous breast;
His altar is the pious heart.

licence: Public domain: James Edward Smith died in 1828.
credits: Words by James Edward Smith (1759–1828), public domain, as printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion (1853); set to WINCHESTER NEW by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
